Congrats on the launch. Adding a memory layer to LLMs is a real painpoint. I've been experimenting with mem0 and it solves a real problem that I failed to solve myself, and we're going to use it in production.
Memory is extremely useful and almost a requirement when it comes to building next level agents and Mem0 is probably the best designed/easiest way to get there.
Looks very over engineered to me.
I observed at least two brand new accounts posting some variety of "kudos", not flagged into oblivion (yet). Gives me the ick, i guess it's better to know mem0 is a shady marketer.
If I see this many questions that could have been taken straight from an FAQ, all followed up with 'great question, we do so and so..', my alarm bells go off. Shady marketing indeed.
Not sure if I'm seeing a clear value prop here. Why is this something that model providers won't build themselves? Can you link some clear use-cases/killer apps that leverage mem0?

We looked at Mem0, Letta/MemGPT, and similar memory solutions. They all solve storing facts from conversations - key-value memory with semantic search. Useful, but not what we needed - Mem0 doesn't learn patterns implicitly from user behavior.
